This National Apprenticeship Week I challenge all of you to get involved and help spread the word. Host an apprenticeship event. Visit one in your community or issue an apprenticeship proclamation. We want everyone to recognize the power of registered apprentices which help hardworking Americans excel in meaningful careers. The future of our country is in the hands of our skilled workers. Together let's celebrate the hardworking men and women who are building a stronger nation. So this National Apprenticeship Week thank you for all you do to help put American workers first in our quest to make America skilled again.

As my dear friend, the late great Charlie Kirk put it, all law reflects a morality. Neither law nor morality appears in a vacuum, but ultimately come from religion. And the morality and religion that formed the American consciousness were decidedly Christian, founded upon the principles and the divinity of Jesus Christ. In 1783, Washington also proclaimed that imitation of divine charity is necessary for the mutual affection of our citizenry and the happiness of our nation. If we do not see that God loves us, we have little reason and little inspiration to love one another. This love which forms our morality is the foundation of a peaceful and healthful society. Many major events have tested the U.S. military over our 250-year history.  

This week, we reflect on what prepared @usarmy Gen. John Pershing for the battlefields of WWI, the heroism of four chaplains during the sinking of a WWII transport ship & the Tet Offensive in Vietnam. https://t.co/YT5yNEEAj0

transcript.text: Welcome to this week's reflective moments of America's military, a weekly segment where we take you through the US military's 250-year history. On January 30, 1968, over 80,000 North Vietnamese and Viet Cong troops launched a surprise on more than 100 cities and towns across South Vietnam, ranging from provincial capitals to the US Embassy in Saigon. However, US forces and South Vietnamese troops responded to the attacks, beat back the offensive, and eventually recaptured the territory. On February 3, 1943, the US Army transport doorchester, a former coastal passenger steamship requisitioned by the Army crossed the Northern Atlantic and was struck by a German torpedo. As the ship sank, four Army chaplains, ministers George L. Fox and Clark V. Poling, priest John P. Washington and Rabbi Alexander B. Goat, began tending to soldiers and guiding them to safety. As lifefests ran out, the chaplains each chose to give theirs to another soldier, in an act that would earn them all a posthumous, distinguished service cross and purple heart. On February 5, 1917, following a year-long expedition deep into the heart of Mexico, in search of Mexican revolutionary leader Pachovia, Army general John Blackjack Pershing, and his troops crossed back into the United States after being recalled. The expedition provided experience in mobilization and logistics, particularly in the use of motorized vehicles and aircraft. These skills would prove invaluable soon on the battlefields of Europe as the US was on the verge of entering World War I. This has been this week's reflective moments of America's military. Visit our website for more information and be sure to check back next week for more.
